pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind cleanup
/sig scheduling

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

- [x] Move Policy API from `pkg/scheduler/api` to `pkg/scheduler/apis/config` (unversioned) and `staging/src/k8s.io/kube-scheduler/config/v1` (versioned and can be vendored externally by end-users).
- [x] dual-register Policy as apiGroup "v1" and "kubescheduler.config.k8s.io".
    - [ ] Unit test verifying both legacy "v1" group and new "kubescheduler.config.k8s.io" can both serialized properly.
    - [ ] Deprecate Policy API with apiGroup "v1".
- [x] Move existing validation and compatibility code to `pkg/scheduler/apis/config`.
- [x] Eliminate `latest.Codec`; use `scheme.Codecs` instead.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #82390

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

- As the legacy Policy API doesn't have XYZList defined, and this PR doesn't add new API fields (just move), so a series of exception rules are added.
- The only file left under `pkg/scheduler/api` is `pkg/scheduler/api/well_known_labels.go`. We will use another PR to find a good place to move those const strings.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
The scheduler v1 Policy API is now enforced with a standard apiGroup `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io`. Policy API can be vendored via `k8s.io/scheduler`.
```

issue_context.title: Move all scheduler API-related code to a single place
issue_context.body:
Currently there are two api packages in the scheduler: [scheduler/api](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/api/) and [scheduler/apis](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/apis/), we should move everything under scheduler/api to scheduler/apis:
 
1) configuration-related APIs, specifically Policy, should be moved to apis/config, it should be under v1 though, and should be double register under both ```apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1``` and ```apiVersion: v1```

2) extender-related apis should move to apis/extenders

/sig scheduling
comments:
`scheduler/apis` makes sense.

`api` folder exists in API machinery due to historic reason, that folder doesn't represent another api instead of the core API.

@ahg-g @Huang-Wei I'd like to take this task.
/assign

Hi @danielqsj It seems like a big Job !
Can you break down some sub-tasks? Then more people can help with this.

This belongs to a line item called "API Cleanup" in the next release cycle. We will first define the overall scope and then divide it into several pieces for contributors who are interested to pick up.

Thanks Daniel, during the sig meeting yesterday @Huang-Wei expressed interest in owning this umbrella item.

/assign @Huang-Wei
It will make Code structure more clearly，but why do k8s put them in two path at the first time?

> It will make Code structure more clearly，but why do k8s put them in two path at the first time?

Historical reasons.

@ProgramerGu for some historical reason, we don't have the concept of `apiGroup`; we just have `apiVersion`, that's what the path `/api` came into, which now represents a "particular" group called "core group". While along with the Kubernetes development, `apiGroup` was brought up and each API resource has its GVK (group, version, kind). So since then `/apis` aggregates all the resources which have explicit "gropu" info.

BTW: the "apiVersion" in `pod.spec.apiVersion` actually means "apiGroupVersion". It's not changed also due to the same historical reason.

The other reason is that config APIs under apis/config are published [under a separate external repo](https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-scheduler) that provides external, versioned API types that can be vendored and used by third-party code instead of vendoring the scheduler code directly.

review_comments: I think we shouldn't make those part of the API, I suggest we move them somewhere else internal, otherwise we will be stuck with supporting them.
I suppose you meant to comment this on `staging/src/k8s.io/kube-scheduler/config/v1/types.go`? (`pkg/scheduler/apis/config/types.go` is for internal usage.)
either both places or just staging. It depends on what we plan to do with the extender API as well.
The extender APIs declared below (everything from to the end of the file) are not part of the scheduler config, I think it should go under apis/extender

Yup, we discussed this offline earlier. I agree semantically they're not part of scheduler CC. However, when I started the implementation, I found out that moving these fields to `apis/extender` will get it promoted to be the top-level API. So in API machinery and codegen's perspective, we might need to embed `metav1.TypeMeta` - which I'm not sure is the conventional way to proceed. So let's get API experts' option on this first.
